title: `<link rel=stylesheet>` waits for critical subresources before we know what they are
body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

The [spec](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/semantics.html#fetching-and-processing-a-resource-from-a-link-element:critical-subresources) for `<link>` requires us to wait for the style sheet's critical subresources to load before processing the resource. ie, to load any style resources before creating a `CSSStyleSheet`:

> 3. Otherwise, wait for the [link resource](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/links.html#external-resource-link)'s [critical subresources](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/infrastructure.html#critical-subresources) to finish loading.
> 4. [Process the linked resource](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/semantics.html#process-the-linked-resource) given el, success, response, and bodyBytes.

At that point, step 3, we don't know what those subresources are, because we haven't parsed the CSS, we just have a byte sequence. The encoding for the CSS is not determined until step 4.1 of [process the linked resource](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/links.html#link-type-stylesheet:process-the-linked-resource) which is step 4 quoted above.

Related to #2997.
